text:
sam_h: FYI — Pegasus (customer) ran into p50 latency spikes with 8k seq using the new 4-bit quant kernel. They want a plan for next sprint to hit p50 <= 220ms for typical chat flows.

maria_g: ouch. do we have repro? input seq distribution?

sam_h: they sent a small trace and perf runs. looks like adapter-heavy prompts + longer histories. KV cache miss rate up ~3x when switching kernels. attached logs in support ticket.

dave_r: quick thought — quant kernel reduces per-token compute but changes memory access patterns. if KV layout differs we can hurt streaming p50. we should scope: is this a kernel change, KV policy, or routing fallback?

maria_g: agree. propose we draft a short PRD: scope, acceptance criteria, rollout plan, canary metrics, and an emergency fallback. owner?

sam_h: I'll own PRD / customer comms. can we get an eng runtime owner for technical specs? @xing_zh?

xing_zh: I can take the kernel/KV investigation. initial triage today: reproduce perf with customer prompt set locally, run both kernels and capture cache hit/miss and latency tail.

dave_r: for acceptance criteria, suggest: p50 <= 220ms, p95 <= 420ms, no regression vs baseline on overall throughput > -5%, and KV miss rate delta <= +1.5%. if can't meet, automatic routing to fallback kernel for that model/tenant.
maria_g: +1. Also add rollout gates: canary at 2% traffic, monitor p50/p95, KV_miss_rate, cost delta, and an auto-abort if p95 increases > 10% or KV_miss>2%.
xing_zh: plan for experiments: create perf harness like below and run at 8k seq distribution.

```bash
# reproduce run
python infra/bench/run_perf.py --model redwood-quant-4b --seq 8192 --batch 1 --prompts data/pegasus_prompts.json --collect-kv-stats
```

Also will instrument runtime to emit kv.cache.hits and kv.cache.misses per request (low overhead metric).

sam_h: for customer impact, they said 60% of requests are short (<=512) and 40% long (>2k) with long histories. can we confine routing rule to only long-history requests?

dave_r: yes, routing by sequence-length + tenant tag is straightforward. config example:

```yaml
routing_policies:
  - name: pegasus-long-history-fallback
    match:
      tenant: pegasus
      approx_sequence_length: ">=2048"
    route_to: kernel-compat
    fallback_on: kv_miss_rate > 0.02
```

maria_g: edge cases: streaming clients that upgrade mid-request, or cached prefixes served from different kernel variants. add test for prefix-compatibility: ensure tokens generated by fallback kernel match behaviorally (no hallucination regressions).
xing_zh: we'll add a prompt-level regression suite with ~200 prompts and acceptance thresholds (exact-match for structured outputs where applicable, and ±token-level similarity for open generation).
sam_h: timeline? customer wants plan this week; can we have PRD + triage notes by EOD Friday, then prototype next sprint?
dave_r: realistic: triage + metrics by Fri EOD, PRD draft by Mon, prototype next sprint, canary in week after if prototype stable.
maria_g: owners: sam_h (product / customer), xing_zh (eng runtime lead), dave_r (SRE/ops & rollout policy). I'll help write acceptance criteria and rollout checklist.

infra-bot: deploy-checklist triggered: please ensure the canary dashboard contains these metrics — latency.p50, latency.p95, kv.cache.hits, kv.cache.misses, cost.tokens_per_sec.

sam_h: noted. I'll file the RFC/PRD: /docs/rfcs/pegasus-kernel-kv-fallback-2172.md and ping reviewers. tagging @eng-runtime for visibility :eyes:

maria_g: thanks — please include a small rollback playbook and a customer communication snippet.
xing_zh: starting triage now. will post perf artifacts in thread when ready. :thumbsup:
